svg.title: One event loop per worker. Block it and everyone waits.
svg.desc: A request path from socket through uvicorn, Starlette and FastAPI to your handler, feeding a single event loop drawn as a circle inside a dashed worker-process boundary. Three branches leave the loop: an async handler that awaits and yields at 470 requests per second, an async handler containing a blocking call which is crossed out in red at 16.9 requests per second, and a plain def handler served by a forty-thread pool at 538. Bars at concurrency 200 compare 2565, 655 and 16.9 requests per second.
svg.text: One event loop per worker. Block it and everyone waits.
async def + await -> it yields, the loop serves others
async def + a BLOCKING call -> the loop freezes
plain def -> handed to a pool of 40 threads
the ceiling is 40 concurrent blocking handlers.
--workers N gives you N of these, and N times the memory
/ping = 3 536 rps - that is the stack's own ceiling
